# The Rule, and Why It Is First

At the top of this collection's global instructions:

> **Before you do any work, mention how you could verify that work.**

--

Two properties a plan gets from being stated *before*:

- it cannot be fitted to whatever came out
- it is run by something other than the author's reasoning: a test, a render read back, a second agent, a number recomputed from the source

--

The running example: adding the exclusion rule from module 2's `SPEC.md` to `data/trip_metrics.R`. Three planted bad rows must be dropped before any metric is computed.

---
name: self-check

# Why "I Verified It" Is Not Verification

A fleet build (2026-09): seven slide decks, one agent each, every agent told to render and self-verify.

--

**7 of 7 passed their self-checks. 7 of 7 had real visual breakage.**

--

The builder cannot see the page it reasons about unless it rasterizes and reads it. Even then it is anchored on what it meant to produce.

--

The report of completion reads the same either way. A diff, a test, a rasterized page, a recomputed number: none of those have a tone.

---

# Three Levels of Check

**Existence.** The file is there, the render finished, exit 0. Necessary, never sufficient. Most false positives live here.

--

**Correctness.** The artifact has the property the spec names. A test asserts it; a golden output matches; a page read back shows the title and no clipping; a render-time `stopifnot()` ties a number to the pipeline.

--

**Intent.** The change does what was asked and nothing else. The diff is the size of the request. A verifier that did not write it re-derives the key numbers from the raw source.

--

A plan names the level of each row. "Rendered without errors" is existence. "Page 12 rasterized and read, title present, last text row above 700 px" is correctness.

---
name: plan-table

# The Plan Is a Table

| Artifact | Check | Level | What failure looks like |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trip_metrics.R` | runs on `trips.csv` | existence | non-zero exit |
| output | first line: "3 rows excluded" | correctness | any other count |
| output | per-city `trips` sum to 4997 | correctness | 5000: rule not applied |
| output | `median_fare` still present | correctness | column missing |
| diff | one filter + one print, nothing else | intent | any other hunk |

--

The last column is the discipline. If you cannot say what failure would look like, the row is not a check. "Looks right" is existence pretending to be correctness.

--

Give the table to Claude in the prompt. The docs say the same from the cost side: a verification target lets the agent catch its own misses before you pay to request fixes.

---

# Checks That Work (1): Render, Then Read

For anything visual: slides, a PDF page, a web page.

```bash
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless \
  --print-to-pdf=/tmp/deck.pdf "file://$PWD/slides.html?print-pdf"
Rscript -e 'png::writePNG(pdftools::pdf_render_page("/tmp/deck.pdf", 12, dpi = 150), "/tmp/p12.png")'
```

then **Read the PNG**. Look for a missing title, clipped bottom text, literal `$x$` where math should be, a footer button over a box.

--

What does not work: `grep` on the rendered HTML. xaringan embeds the whole source, escaped, so every tag and every computed value is "present" even when the slide renders wrong.

--

Sanity on the PNG itself: a slide is 80 to 130 KB; under 40 KB is a load failure; several pages with the same byte count are all the page-1 fallback.

---

# Checks That Work (2): Golden Output and Re-derivation

**Golden output.** Same input, before and after, diff the outputs. For a change that *should* alter the output, predict the delta first:

> three fewer rows; mean fare moves by less than a cent; the excluded count prints as 3

--

**Independent re-derivation.** A fresh agent, given the raw source and **not** the author's conclusion, recomputes each number.

In a review loop this caught a hand-written annotation that was wrong while every computed number passed. Verify annotations, not just computations.

--

**Render-time assertion.** In a slide chunk:

```r
stopifnot(sum(metrics$trips) == nrow(clean_trips))
```

Drift fails the render instead of shipping.

---
name: definition-check

# Checks That Work (3): The Definition, Not the Value

A derived number can be right for the wrong reason.

--

A macro `FileDrawerPostExpl` = 48% was defined as `file_drawer - explained` (58 − 10.3: what is still missing). A draft cited it to mean "availability rose to about 48%" (42 + 6.2 = 48.2).

--

Both round to 48. The macro would have been **numerically right and semantically wrong**, and a value comparison passes it.

--

Habit: before citing a derived number, grep its pipeline definition. If two plausible computations land on the same rounded value, state which one the macro actually is.

A second instance the same month: "18% of missing hypotheses explained" versus a table's "18.2% of explanations" are different quantities. Find the table that computes the claim before calling it inconsistent.

---
name: lies-1

# Checks That Lie (1): Stale, Silent, Not-Really-Done

Each reported success on a failure in a real session.

--

**The stale artifact.** `until [ -f /tmp/out.png ]; do sleep 1; done` exits at once on yesterday's file; the downstream `Read` inspects an old render and reports success. `rm -f` the target before polling, or compare `mtime` to the source.

--

**The silent no-op.** `perl -pe 's/\x{2014}/-/g'` without `-CSD` matches nothing and exits 0. BSD `sed` has no `\b`, so `sed -i 's/\bAI\b/x/'` exits 0 and changes nothing. Check that bytes changed, not that the command succeeded.

--

**The wrong "completed".** `cmd > log 2>&1 &` with `run_in_background` reports done when the *wrapper* exits. A background agent's "completed" can be a session-limit death at near-zero tokens. Tail the log; glance at the usage block.

<a href="#lies-detail" class="nav-btn">four more →</a>

---

# Checks That Lie (2): The Half-Run Chain

```bash
cd proj && export BIBINPUTS=... && pdflatex main; bibtex main; pdflatex main
```

`cd` fails (already there, cwd reset by the harness). The `&&` chain aborts before the export. **Every `;`-separated command still runs**, now without the variable. Bibtex finds no databases; the "undefined citation" warnings look like a document bug.

--

Same family, the other direction:

```bash
grep -c 'TODO' README.md && git commit -m "clean"   # zero matches is the GOOD result
```

`grep -c` exits 1 on zero. The commit is skipped. The good result silently blocked the step after it.

--

Rule: diagnostics and mutations in separate calls. Make a whole chain `&&`, or export on its own line first.

---

# Summary

| Do | Because |
|---|---|
| State the plan before the prompt, as a table | it cannot be fitted to the result |
| One column for "what failure looks like" | a row without it is not a check |
| At least one row that recomputes a number from data | messages the code prints about itself pass bugs |
| Render and *read*; never grep rendered HTML | the source is embedded, escaped, always "present" |
| Confirm a change by bytes or diff, not exit code | silent no-ops exit 0 |
| Confirm "absent" with a second tool | the search tool has lied before |
| Give the table to Claude in the prompt | it catches its own misses before you pay for a fix |

--

The drill writes the table for the exclusion rule, injects a bug, and shows which row catches it and which plan would have passed it.

name: lies-detail

# Backup: Four More Checks That Lie

.small[
**The false-negative search.** `grep` on this machine is `ugrep`. Twice in one session it returned nothing for a phrase that was in the file (a `.tex` under `grep -rn --include='*.tex'`; a `\url{}` match), nearly producing a wrong "not in the source." Before concluding absence, confirm with `python3 -c "print('phrase' in open(f).read())"`. A context pattern like `.\{0,90\}word.\{0,60\}` over a large file fails with "exceeds complexity limits".

**The print-to-PDF dropout.** Chrome's print can drop the final `--` reveal on a `class: center, middle` slide, or collapse every `count: false` group and every build to one page. If an untouched baseline slide shows the identical truncation it is the tool, not the edit. Reliable per-state check: remark's `#N` addresses the Nth generated state; compute N from the `.Rmd` and screenshot `slides.html#N`.

**Low-DPI misreads.** A 42-dpi raster made "826,216" read as "B26,216". Fine for layout; before flagging a digit or a word, re-render that region at 150 dpi and crop.

**The Edit that cannot find what Write just wrote.** An `old_string` copied verbatim from a file created seconds earlier fails with "not found." Re-read once after a `Write` before editing, or rewrite the whole file. Same symptom when a background agent edited the file after your last read, or when the `old_string` spans two distant copies of a repeated block (use `replace_all` on the short identical line).
]
